what: The exact one-pass cooperative test (experiments/vllm_exact_receipts.py) repeated on a dense BF16 model, Qwen/Qwen3-8B (thinking off via chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking=false), on two rented GPUs of different generations: an RTX 4090 (Ada, Vast, driver 580.178.04) and an RTX 3090 (Ampere, Vast, driver 580.173.02). Each ran vLLM 0.32.0 (torch 2.13.0) with VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, eager, max-model-len 4096 and the llmverify logits processor; each made its own determinism run (48 prompts, sequential and 16 concurrent, vllm_determinism.py) and its own signed receipts (48 prompts x greedy / T=1.0 / T=0.7 top-p 0.95, max 200 tokens, plus tampered copies), and each checked the other's receipts in one prefill pass.
determinism: rtx4090 and rtx3090: sequential vs 16 concurrent 0 of 8,250 positions differ on each; rtx4090 vs rtx3090: 0 of 8,250 positions differ (top-20 logprobs to 1e-4 nats), sequential and concurrent
same_machine_checks: identical counts on each box (0 honest positions differ; every tampered reply flagged first at the flip)
notes: 143 tampered replies per provider, not 144: one T=0.7 top-p 0.95 reply (19 tokens) had no position where the rule had a runner-up inside the nucleus, so no edit was possible. Sampled honest replies differ between the two providers only because each receipt carries its own random client nonce. Together with the gpt-oss-20b result (vllm-exact-receipts-gpt-oss-20b.json) the exact tier on vLLM now holds for a MoE MXFP4 model and a dense BF16 model, across Ampere and Ada.
